name: PUBLISHERS
reason: Host wiring: an id-keyed table of factories the embedding host registers at startup (core::slots::HookSlot). It holds code, never tenant data; a per-context override table lives on the CoreContext, not here.

name: MEMORY
reason: Process-local in-memory attachment fallback only for the CLI/direct/test path without init_attachments_dir; the host path uses the initialized workspace-backed stash instead. Avoids persisting bytes or credentials on disk and is never selected for initialized service workspaces.
verification: agent/multimodal.rs: stash() selects workspace-scoped attachment_stash_for(workspace) when ATTACHMENTS_DIR is initialized; memory_stash() is the explicitly ephemeral uninitialized fallback. Never expose a shared fallback for multi-tenant services.

name: OPEN_WORKSPACE_STORES
reason: Holds open the workspace transcript stores used when no host session store is installed. Each entry is a handle to the SQLite store under one workspace, keyed by that workspace and the session store key (agent_key_for: <profile>~<agent> for a SaaS profile), so two profiles or agents never share an entry; the store under the workspace is the authoritative data. release_workspace_defaults drops them all for a data reset, release_workspace those of one workspace.

name: PROCESS
reason: The process's registry of weak handles to the rebindable session-store providers a host installed, so a workspace switch (storage::rebind) can point each at the new backend. It holds no records and no tenant state, only Weak references; the stores' data lives in the storage backend. A test builds its own StoreRegistry, so rebinding one never moves another's stores.

name: CALLBACKS
reason: Host wiring: an id-keyed table of factories the embedding host registers at startup (core::slots::HookSlot). It holds code, never tenant data; a per-context override table lives on the CoreContext, not here.

name: BUILTIN_CLOUD_PROVIDERS
reason: Immutable process-wide provider preset definitions converted from upstream builtin declarations plus host-owned presets. Contains no account, workspace, token or user data.
verification: config/schema/cloud_providers_tests.rs: built-in provider contracts; cloud_providers.rs constructs the table solely from constants.

name: TEST_GLOBALS
reason: cfg(test) only: replaces a slot's process table with a per-thread one so a test's fake registration cannot reach a test on another thread. Not compiled into any shipped build.

name: SERVED
reason: Caches one document callback address per workspace, storage scope and explicit backend identity. Each target resolves only its bound scope and rejects collections outside the schedule contract; no job or credential payload is cached here.

name: KIND_REGISTRY_TEST_LOCK
reason: cfg(test) only: serializes tests that read, replace and use the process-wide job-kind handler registry. The mutex contains only unit and is held until the temporary registration has dropped; it stores no tenant state and is absent from shipped builds.

name: REGISTRY
reason: Process-wide host registration table for job-kind and named system handlers. The handler receives the execution binding explicitly through JobRunContext; registrations and drop order select host code, not a tenant credential or job store.

name: LOOP_RUNNING
reason: A process-wide admission bit for the single scheduler polling loop. LoopSlot releases it on drop; it stores no scope, job data or authorization decision.

name: MANUAL_RUNS
reason: Process-wide manual-run admission fence containing job identifiers only. A matching id serializes manual attempts across the process; it does not grant access to that job or choose its storage scope. RunGuard removes the entry on drop, including cancellation.

name: REG
reason: Single-process suppression of repeated provider credential errors by provider slug; contains transient in-memory error states but no credential bytes. API consumers must keep this single-user diagnostic state out of multi-tenant authorization decisions.
verification: inference/auth_error_registry.rs records and clears failed episodes by provider; no authenticated token values are stored in this structure.

name: RESOLVER
reason: Process-wide model context-window estimate cache keyed by provider/model; holds numeric token-window hints rather than user prompts, tokens or individual messages.
verification: inference/context_window.rs: remembered_window(provider, model) delegates to tinyinference-llm resolver; no credentials are passed to the cache.

name: POOLS
reason: BYOK credential health and bounded run-affinity state are keyed by the explicitly supplied workspace/provider/model scope. Hosted profiles receive distinct workspace paths from ProfileHost::forced_config and profile_config for their validated ProfileId; status/reset use the config bound to DispatchCtx, and CredentialFleetModel retains its construction scope for outcomes and lease release. Agents in one workspace intentionally share provider health. The pool stores salted key IDs, counters, deadlines and bounded run IDs, not plaintext credentials; the trusted host must preserve each profile's workspace binding.
verification: profiles/layout_tests.rs: the_config_is_rooted_in_the_profile_and_bound_to_its_memory; profiles/types_proptest_tests.rs: distinct_users_get_distinct_ids, layout_dir_is_one_segment_under_users; config/ops/loader_explicit_ctx_tests.rs: concurrent_loads_never_see_each_others_config; inference/provider/factory/key_pool_tests.rs: pool_retains_only_salted_key_ids_not_raw_secrets, deleted_model_scope_does_not_remove_sibling_key_health; inference/provider/factory/cloud_slug.rs: fleet_scope; inference/provider/factory.rs: model_fleet_health and model_fleet_reset

name: SALT
reason: A process-created random SipHash seed used to derive transient credential identifiers. The OnceLock holds only RandomState, never the input credentials or per-tenant health records; those identifiers remain inside the separately scoped POOLS entries.
verification: inference/provider/factory/key_pool.rs: secret_id initializes RandomState::new and hashes the borrowed input without retaining it; inference/provider/factory/key_pool_tests.rs: pool_retains_only_salted_key_ids_not_raw_secrets

name: NEXT_QNML_CALL
reason: Numeric process sequence used only to synthesize QNML call IDs together with the process ID. It stores no prompt, arguments, credentials, tenant identity or authorization state; the request's declared tool schema still validates each generated call.

name: NEXT_TAGGED_CALL
reason: Numeric process sequence used only to synthesize tagged-JSON call IDs together with the process ID. It contains no call payload or tenant state and grants no tool authority; decode_calls validates against the tools declared for that request.

name: CLIENTS
reason: The canonical TinyMCP client table is keyed by the resolved agent directory. Host completion and exact-client eviction preserve the same directory fence across close and purge; no runtime guard is retained in the table.

name: LIFECYCLE_GATE
reason: Serializes TinyMCP open/close transitions, which the module admits one at a time process-wide; it guards no data and carries no tenant state.

name: STORE
reason: Every entry key is prefixed with the calling tenant's profile and agent scope through tenant_key, and a SaaS call with no tenant scope gets an isolated key that never matches.

name: ENGINES

reason: Host wiring: an id-keyed table of handlers the embedding host registers at startup (core::slots::HookSlot). It holds code, never tenant data; a per-context override table lives on the CoreContext, not here.

name: ROUTE_TURN
reason: Test-only (cfg(test)): serializes each TinyConnectors call with the route it sets, because libtest runs a crate's tests in one process and the module's route is process-global; it guards no data and carries no tenant state.

name: DONE
reason: Deduplicates successful legacy module imports per importer type, module-scope identity and absolute data directory, using an async gate. A cancelled or failed import is not cached.
verification: modules/mod.rs: import_once caches (kind, module_id, directory) only after a settled successful import.

name: LOGGED
reason: Registry ids whose serving source was already logged, so each is logged once; holds static ids only.

name: TABLE
reason: The compiled module registry in the shape the tinybus resolver consumes; constants only.

name: REPORTER
reason: Deduplicates terminal module outcomes per (module id, reason) so a broken install is one Sentry event per process; keys are registry ids only and no tenant data is held.

name: CALLBACKS
reason: Records that the host callback objects were served on the module bus once, before any module loads; infrastructure only.

name: RUNTIME
reason: The single tinybus module bus (broker, loader, connection) for the process; tinybus never unloads a module, so there is exactly one. Carries no tenant data: tenant scope is resolved per call by the host callbacks it serves.

name: ATTACHED
reason: Test-only attachment result for the linked TinyFlows fixture, initialized once on the process module bus. The production build uses the registry release loader; this fixture records neither job data nor tenant credentials.
verification: modules/tinyflows_fixture.rs: attach is included only from the cfg(test) fixture path in modules/tinyflows.rs

name: HANDLERS
reason: Host wiring: an id-keyed table of handlers the embedding host registers at startup (core::slots::HookSlot). It holds code, never tenant data; a per-context override table lives on the CoreContext, not here.

name: FALLBACK_LLM_PERMITS
reason: Test-only semaphore fallback for synchronous tests without a Tokio runtime. Async tests use a runtime-keyed semaphore; no tenant payload is stored.
verification: platform/llm_gate/gate.rs: cfg(test) llm_permits branches on test_state::current_id

name: LLM_PERMITS
reason: One process-wide semaphore bounds concurrent LLM work for host resource protection. Permits carry no user content or credentials; tests use per-runtime state.

name: RESUME_NOTIFY
reason: Process wake-up signal for background loops. A wake only prompts a fresh policy check and never carries tenant state or grants permission to execute.
verification: platform/llm_gate/gate.rs: update_config and set_signed_out notify on resume, consumers recheck current_policy

name: SIGNED_OUT
reason: Desktop operator-session pause flag only. SaaS reads always return false and SaaS writes are rejected, so one tenant expiry cannot pause other tenants; no credential bytes are retained.
verification: platform/llm_gate/gate.rs: signed_out_with and accepts_signed_out_write_with explicitly exclude SaaS

name: STARTED
reason: Starts the single host resource sampler exactly once. It contains no tenant data; later scheduler policy updates use update_config.
verification: platform/llm_gate/gate.rs: init_global initializes STATE and spawns the sampler only inside call_once

name: STATE
reason: Cached host scheduler policy and sampled power/resource signals. GateCore holds SchedulerGateConfig and Signals, not tenant messages or keys; individual credentials remain checked by their owners.

name: REGISTRY
reason: The immutable composition of owner-declared storage schemas. It caches collection/stream/blob declarations and composition errors, not a backend, persisted rows or tenant scope.

name: ARTIFACT_ROW_HANDLE
reason: Keeps the one process-wide event-bus subscription that writes artifact rows alive and makes registration idempotent; it holds no data, and each event names the workspace and thread its row is written to.

name: REGISTRY
reason: Keyed by a random per-remix correlation id; each entry holds the registering caller's config and CoreContext, which every callback re-enters. Callbacks are accepted only from the module peer (bus name owner) for a live id, and the entry is retired by End, a failed call, or an age sweep.

name: FOREGROUND
reason: Holds only unit mutexes. The key is the workspace directory, so different workspaces never share or wait on a lock and no tenant data is stored.

name: PATTERN
reason: Six function-local caches contain immutable compiled regular expressions initialized only from hard-coded Rust, JavaScript and Python syntax patterns. Source documents, captures and graph results remain local to each bounded graph call and are never stored in these caches.
